subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Events A and B are mutually exclusive with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.3. What is P(A or B)?
questions.explain: For mutually exclusive events P(A or B) = 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7.

questions.q: A coin is flipped 200 times and lands heads 90 times. What is the experimental probability of heads?
A pie chart represents 40 people in 360°. How many degrees represent one person?
How many outcomes are in the sample space when rolling two fair six-sided dice?
In a frequency table, the value 3 occurs 5 times and the value 4 occurs 2 times. What is the mode?
questions.explain: The value with the highest frequency is 3 (occurring 5 times).

questions.q: For grouped data with classes 0-10, 10-20, 20-30 having frequencies 4, 9, 2, which is the modal class?
questions.explain: The class with the highest frequency (9) is 10-20.

questions.q: Two fair coins are flipped. What is P(both heads)?
A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is P(rolling a 4)?
questions.explain: There is one favourable outcome out of six equally likely: 1/6.

questions.q: The probability it rains is 0.3. What is the probability it does not rain?
In a tree diagram, the first branch shows P = 0.6 and a following branch shows P = 0.5. What is the probability of both happening?
